title: School dropout’s AI start-up valued at £2.5bn
excerpt: A British start-up founded by a 25-year-old school dropout has been valued at £2.5bn as it develops new chips for the AI boom.
content_html:
A British start-up founded by a 25-year-old school dropout has been valued at £2.5bn as it develops new chips for the AI boom.

Olix, led by James Dacombe, an entrepreneur, raised $312m (£232m) from investors as it looks to compete against Nvidia in the market for high-tech chips.

The deal values Olix at $3.3bn, tripling its valuation since February, when the start-up raised a further $220m.

Mr Dacombe started Olix two years ago when he was just 23, having launched his first company as a teenager after dropping out of his sixth form college in Harrogate, just two days into starting his A-levels.

He launched his first company, CoMind, a brain-scanning business, at the age of 17 in 2018, and continues to work as its chief executive as well as running Olix.

Mr Dacombe was made a fellow of billionaire Peter Thiel's charitable foundation in 2022, which provides grants to young entrepreneurs who drop out of college to launch startups.

His new start-up is working to develop faster microchips to lower the costs of AI and now employs more than 140 staff across London, Bristol, Canada and the US.

The start-up says its chip designs, which rely on beams of light to move data instead of copper such as a traditional semiconductor, can help "unlock a step change in AI performance and cost".

Investors in Olix's latest funding round included Cambridge semiconductor giant Arm, Reed Hastings, the Netflix founder and Hudson River Trading, the US trading firm.

It also secured backing from the Government's £500m Sovereign AI Fund, set up under Labour to invest in promising technology companies in an effort to keep them in the UK.

A series of new British start-ups has raised hundreds of millions of pounds this year as venture investors seek to capitalise on booming demand for AI chips.

Fractile, a Bristol start-up, raised $220m in May this year in a fundraising round led by Mr Thiel's Founders Fund, which was an early investor in tech giants, including SpaceX, Palantir and Facebook.

CuspAI, a start-up using AI to discover new materials for chip design, secured $450m last week from investors, including Jeff Bezos.

Alongside the funding, Olix said it had appointed Prof Nick McKeown, a Stanford University electronics expert, to its board, while Nick Briers, a former executive at the financial technology business Wise, had joined as its chief financial officer.

Kanishka Narayan, the AI minister, said: "Olix is exactly the kind of ambitious company we want to back through Sovereign AI."

content_html_zh:
一家由 25 岁辍学青年创立的英国初创公司为人工智能热潮开发新芯片，估值达 25 亿英镑。

Olix 由企业家 James Dacombe 领导，从投资者那里筹集了 3.12 亿美元（2.32 亿英镑），以期在高科技芯片市场与 Nvidia 展开竞争。

此次交易对 Olix 的估值为 33 亿美元，是自 2 月份以来这家初创公司进一步筹集 2.2 亿美元的估值的两倍。

两年前，Dacombe 先生创办了 Olix，当时他年仅 23 岁。十几岁的时候，他从哈罗盖特的六年级学院退学，开始 A-level 考试仅两天后，就创办了自己的第一家公司。

2018 年，17 岁时，他创办了自己的第一家公司 CoMind，一家脑部扫描公司，并继续担任该公司的首席执行官并运营 Olix。

Dacombe 先生于 2022 年成为亿万富翁 Peter Thiel 慈善基金会的会员，该基金会为大学辍学创办初创企业的年轻企业家提供资助。

他的新初创公司致力于开发更快的微芯片以降低人工智能成本，目前在伦敦、布里斯托尔、加拿大和美国拥有 140 多名员工。

这家初创公司表示，其芯片设计依靠光束而不是传统半导体等铜来移动数据，可以帮助“实现人工智能性能和成本的阶跃变化”。

Olix 最新一轮融资的投资者包括剑桥半导体巨头 Arm、Netflix 创始人 Reed Hastings 和美国贸易公司 Hudson River Trading。

它还获得了政府 5 亿英镑的主权人工智能基金的支持，该基金是工党领导下设立的，旨在投资有前途的科技公司，努力将它们留在英国。

随着风险投资者寻求利用人工智能芯片蓬勃发展的需求，一系列新的英国初创企业今年筹集了数亿英镑。

布里斯托尔初创公司 Fractile 在今年 5 月由 Thiel 创始人基金领投的一轮融资中筹集了 2.2 亿美元，该基金是 SpaceX、Palantir 和 Facebook 等科技巨头的早期投资者。

CuspAI 是一家利用人工智能发现芯片设计新材料的初创公司，上周从包括杰夫·贝索斯 (Jeff Bezos) 在内的投资者那里获得了 4.5 亿美元的投资。

除了这笔资金外，Olix 还表示，已任命斯坦福大学电子专家 Nick McKeown 教授为董事会成员，金融科技公司 Wise 前高管 Nick Briers 也加入其担任首席财务官。

人工智能部长 Kanishka Narayan 表示：“Olix 正是我们希望通过 Sovereign AI 支持的那种雄心勃勃的公司。”
